burnham-on-sea.snapshot: Burnham-on-Sea and neighbouring Highbridge sit on the Somerset coast where full fibre and structured cabling keep field engineers busy. Big build contractors run crews on trade accounts and buy kit centrally, while ex-BT sole traders and independent broadband and CCTV installers order direct online with no account. A workwear supplier here has to serve the fleet and the one-van installer alike, side by side.
burnham-on-sea.s1_head: Kitting the field engineers of Somerset
s1loc: Burnham-on-Sea and Highbridge have seen a multi-million pound full fibre build land in recent years, with Openreach passing more than 11,000 homes and businesses across the two towns and the surrounding Sedgemoor villages. Virgin Media O2 has pushed its own ultrafast network out under Project Lightning on top, so the streets, cabinets and customer premises along Berrow Road, Worston and out toward Brent Knoll and East Brent now carry competing networks. The build runs through delivery partners and civils crews, with a steady tail of broadband and CCTV installers picking up the connect work behind them.

Alongside the residential rollout sits a real commercial scene anchored on the Isleport Business Park and Oaktree Business Park at Highbridge, where occupiers like Yeo Valley and Bakkavor Desserts run sizeable sites close to the M5 Junction 22. Structured-cabling and fibre-optic firms wire these warehouses, the distribution units on Pillmore Lane and the offices along Burnham high street in Cat5e, Cat6 and fibre, and CCTV installers cover retail, holiday parks and seafront premises across the town and out toward Bridgwater and Weston-super-Mare.

northwich.s1_head: Kitting the field engineers of Cheshire
s1loc: Northwich has some of the highest alt-net competition in the country, with full fibre reaching the vast majority of premises and well over a dozen providers live across nearly 49,000 homes and businesses. Openreach has built heavily here, even piloting new install methods on the Long Wood Park and Hill Top Farm developments, while Zzoomm has run an eighteen million pound build of its own network through the town. Crews work through Rudheath, Winnington, Castle and Leftwich, so the streets and cabinets carry competing fibre and a steady flow of connect and repair work.

The commercial side is anchored on Gadbrook Park, the hundred-hectare business park at Rudheath, alongside Winnington Business Park and the Wincham Industrial Estate north of the town near the M6. Structured-cabling and fibre-optic firms wire these offices, warehouses and the units off Witton Street in Cat5e, Cat6 and fibre, and CCTV installers cover retail, the chemical-industry sites and multi-site businesses across Northwich and out toward Crewe and Macclesfield.
